claims.text: A hybrid machine-learning interatomic-potential and free-energy-interpolation workflow can provide high-fidelity fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for both solid and liquid phases.
The hybrid workflow will cost roughly an order of magnitude less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The hybrid workflow will cost roughly an order of magnitude less than TOR-TILD.
The proposed cost and fidelity advantages extend to multicomponent high-entropy systems.
A moment tensor potential trained on a selected subset of ab initio data can enable efficient molecular-dynamics sampling.
The enhanced free-energy interpolation can accurately capture anharmonic vibrational contributions.
The enhanced free-energy interpolation can accurately retain electron–vibration coupling.
Combining the surrogate potential with interpolation permits direct evaluation of solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Accurate ML predictions of atomic forces and structural correlations ensure faithful representation of lattice dynamics and anharmonic vibrations.
A sparse but representative ab initio training set is sufficient for an ML potential to reproduce atomic forces and energy surfaces with near-first-principles fidelity.
Near-DFT ML energies and forces enable efficient phase-space sampling while avoiding continuous ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will match explicit ab initio workflows in free-energy, vibrational-entropy, and phase-transition fidelity.
Vibrational entropy varies with temperature and composition in high-entropy alloys.
Anharmonic effects and vibrational entropy become significant under the proposed near-melting conditions.
The workflow is expected to apply to elemental, binary, and moderately complex multicomponent high-entropy alloys when the selected descriptors adequately represent both phases.
Reliability may decline when training data are sparse or predictions extrapolate beyond the training domain.
Reliability may decline for systems with extreme electronic complexity or rare anharmonic events.
Disagreement exceeding 10% in free-energy curves or fusion temperatures relative to full ab initio MD or TOR-TILD is a falsifying outcome.
